notMachineCheckableObligations.N1: Discharged. The two highest-consequence issues were found: the hard invariant that no verifier check moves from pass to fail is broken by the change that declares it (F-001), and the context-slice declarations breach the accepted composition rule while omitting phase-mandatory standards (F-002). F-002 and F-006 were found by independent inspection of the repository and the run record rather than taken from the report's own deviation list, which is the test of whether the review looked or only read.
notMachineCheckableObligations.N2: Discharged. Every finding names a design constraint, a declared invariant, a decision record, a sequencing constraint, or a Phase Model column. notMachineCheckableObligations.N3: Discharged, in both directions. F-004 was held at medium rather than raised to high on positive evidence: the property P-001 was to safeguard was verified directly, both completed reference runs carrying unchanged bytes and timestamps preceding the increment. F-002 was set at high rather than medium only after A-005's enumeration established a violated architecture rule; before that reading, medium was the defensible classification, and the change was made by evidence, not to reach a verdict row.
